title: 2024 HMMT Invitational Problem 2
statement:
Suppose that \(a, b, c\), and \(d\) are real numbers such that \(a+b+c+d=8\). Compute the minimum possible value of

\[20\left(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}+d^{2}\right)-\sum_{\text {sym }} a^{3} b,\]

where the sum is over all 12 symmetric terms.

solutions.text:
Observe that

\[\sum_{\mathrm{sym}} a^{3} b=\sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} a \cdot \sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} a^{3}-\sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} a^{4}=8 \sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} a^{3}-\sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} a^{4}\]

so

\[\begin{aligned}
20 \sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} a^{2}-\sum_{\mathrm{sym}} a^{3} b & =\sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} a^{4}-8 \sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} a^{3}+20 \sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} a^{2} \\
& =\sum_{\mathrm{cyc}}\left(a^{4}-8 a^{3}+20 a^{2}\right) \\
& =16(8)-4(4)+\sum_{\mathrm{cyc}}\left(a^{4}-8 a^{3}+20 a^{2}-16 a+4\right) \\
& =112+\sum_{\mathrm{cyc}}\left(a^{2}-4 a+2\right)^{2} \\
& \geq 112 .
\end{aligned}\]

Equality is achieved when \((a, b, c, d)=(2+\sqrt{2}, 2+\sqrt{2}, 2-\sqrt{2}, 2-\sqrt{2})\) and permutations. This can be checked by noting that for all \(x \in\{a, b, c, d\}\), we have \(x^{2}-4 x+2=0\), so equality holds in the final step, and for this assignment of variables we have \(a+b+c+d=8\).
